# Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta (SN 49)

**ID:** SN 49
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses on the Right Efforts
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn49
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 49), translated as "Linked Discourses on the Right Efforts" or "Connected Discourses on the Right Strivings", is the forty-ninth section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* and forms the fifth chapter of its concluding *Mahāvagga* [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. It represents one of the seven saṁyuttas in the *Mahāvagga* devoted to the fundamental sets of training factors that constitute the Buddhist path to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Bodhi 2003; Gethin 2008].

The collection contains 54 discourses arranged into five vaggas, beginning with the *Gaṅgāpeyyālavagga* and *Appamādavagga* [SuttaCentral; Hazra 1994]. Rather than assembling unique or freestanding suttas, the saṁyutta is structured as a systematic instantiation of the standard repetition series (*peyyāla*) framed around the canonical stock formula of the four right strivings (*cattāro sammappadhānā*) [SuttaCentral; Bodhi 2003]. This formula defines the monk's arousal of desire, effort, energy, and mental striving toward four ends: preventing the arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states, abandoning arisen unwholesome states, arousing unarisen wholesome states, and maintaining and perfecting arisen wholesome states [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. Although numerous discourses treating right effort appear scattered throughout the wider Pali Nikāyas, canonical redactors chose not to collect them here, restricting the saṁyutta to this repetitive schematic treatment [SuttaCentral].

Parallels to portions of the collection survive in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), notably SĀ 875–878 for the *Gaṅgāpeyyālavagga* (SN 49.1–12) and SĀ 882 for the *Appamādavagga* (SN 49.13–22) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus aligns these passages with fascicles 27 and 28 of T 99 and indicates additional cross-language parallels in the Tibetan canonical translations of the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* (D 4094), *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D 3897), and *Aṣṭādaśasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (D 10), as well as the Sanskrit *Śrāvakabhūmi* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus records 988 matching passages across 47 texts, showing extensive textual reuse with the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), other *Mahāvagga* collections (SN 46, SN 47, SN 48, SN 50, SN 51, SN 53), the *Sammappadhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 8), and the *Samaṇamuṇḍika Sutta* (MN 78) [DharmaNexus].
